sentences.text: The petitioner herein was elected as a Councillor from Ward No.24 of Kalaburagi Mahanagara Palike in the elections held in the Month of September 2021.
Her election has been called in question by respondent No.1 herein by filing an Election Petition No.1/2021 before the III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi.

sentences.text: The main ground of challenge is the age of the petitioner and it is contended that she has not yet attained 21 years when the elections were conducted.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 herein has opposed the petition on the ground that the District Court itself is the authority to determine all aspects regarding qualification and disqualification including the eligible age and the question of referring to an authority as demanded by the petitioner herein does not arise.
5. Based on the pleadings and arguments of the parties, the District Court has rejected the application filed by the petitioner herein under Article 243V (2) of the Constitution of India.
Aggrieved by the same, the instant writ petition has been preferred.

6. It is the contention of the petitioner that Article 243V of the Constitution of India speaks about disqualifications for membership and further states that in case of any dispute, the decision shall be referred to such authority as prescribed by the State Legislature and the dispute on hand pertaining to whether the petitioner herein is under aged or not has to be decided by the authority prescribed by the State and cannot be adjudicated by the District Court and the District Court erred in not referring the matter to such authority and has erroneously dismissed the Interlocutory application.
7.
Per contra, learned counsel for the caveator/respondent No.1 has justified the decision of the trial Court.

8. The question that arises for consideration is that if any question arises as to whether the Member of Municipality become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1) of the 243V of the Constitution of India, which is the authority to decide the same.

9. Article 243V of the Constitution of India reads as under:-
"243V. Disqualifications for membership. -
(1) A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of a Municipality - (a) if he is so disqualified by or under any law for the time being in force for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned:
Provided that no person shall be disqualified on the ground that he is less than twenty-five years of age, if he has attained the age of twenty-one years;
(b) if he is so disqualified by or under any law made by the Legislature of the State.
(2) If any question arises as to whether a member of a Municipality has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1), the question shall be referred for the decision of such authority and in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide."

The Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) is enacted to consolidate and amend the laws relating to establishment of Municipal Corporations in the State of Karnataka.

12. Section 33 of the Act speaks about election petition and it reads as under:-
"33. Election petition.

- (1) No election of a councillor shall be called in question except by an election petition presented for adjudication to the District Court having jurisdiction, within thirty days from the date of the publication of the result of election under Section 32.

(2) An election petition may be presented on one or more of the grounds specified in section 35,-
(a) by any candidate at such election; or (b) by any voter of the [ward] concerned.

Thus, as per Section 33 of the Act, any dispute pertaining to election of a Councillor can be called in question before the District Court.
Thus, District Court becomes the authority to decide whether a member of a municipality has become disqualified as contemplated under Article 243V of the Constitution of India.

Thus, if there is a petition filed contending that an elected candidate was not eligible to contest election on the ground that he/she had not attained the prescribed age as per law,
the petition has to be presented before a District Judge and the District Judge is the competent authority to decide the question as to whether the winning candidate has attained the prescribed age or not.
As stated to by learned High Court Government Pleader there is no separate authority prescribed by the State to determine whether a Councillor has attained the prescribed age or not.

13.
